h: Three Things to Know Before an Ipswich Battle
p: First up, Ipswich is easier to reach than plenty of people think. The station sits just south of the town centre across the river, with direct trains from London Liverpool Street, Norwich and Cambridge, so a night out here doesn't need a car. From the station it's a short walk up into town, past the river and towards the busy shopping streets.

Second, think about timing. Ipswich has a solid weekend crowd, and when Ipswich Town are at home the town centre gets that extra matchday buzz. If you're planning around a game, book ahead and expect the bars to be busier than usual. For a quieter evening, an earlier weekday slot tends to be more relaxed, which suits work groups and anyone who wants to hear themselves think.

Third, plan your teams with care. The fun of a games bar comes from close competition, so mix confident players with first-timers and keep the scores visible. Agree a small forfeit for the losers and a modest prize for the winners. Even the most laid-back group tends to get competitive once a trophy, real or imaginary, is up for grabs.

If you want to make a weekend of it, the Suffolk coast is close by. Felixstowe has a long promenade and a working port you can watch from the seafront, while Woodbridge and the Sutton Hoo Anglo-Saxon burial site are a short drive north-east. Sutton Hoo is where the famous ship burial and helmet were found, and it's a fascinating day out before an evening of games back in town.
